examples.trans: That means you simply missed the deadline by a little.

examples.text: У меня нет времени.
examples.trans: I don't have time.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('tight, cramped').

examples.text: Проведём время в тесном семейном кругу.
examples.trans: We will spend time in a close family circle.

examples.text: Пора возвращаться в твою тесную коммуналку.
examples.trans: Time to return to your cramped communal flat.

examples.text: Они жили в маленькой тесной комнате.
examples.trans: They lived in a small cramped room.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'емейный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('family').

examples.text: Проведём время в тесном семейном кругу.
examples.trans: We will spend time in a close family circle.

examples.text: Это семейный праздник.
examples.trans: It's a family holiday.

examples.text: Семейное фото.
examples.trans: A family photo.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'circle, ring, buoy' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Проведём время в тесном семейном кругу.
examples.trans: We will spend time in a close family circle.

examples.text: Ты только посмотри, вокруг все рыжие!
examples.trans: Just look, everyone around here is red-headed!

examples.text: Держись за спасательный круг.
examples.trans: Hold onto the life ring.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'only', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ты только посмотри, вокруг все рыжие!
examples.trans: Just look, everyone around here is red-headed!

examples.text: Но только если жена нас не увидит!
examples.trans: But only if my wife does not see us!

examples.text: Она только что наверх в номер ушла.
examples.trans: She just went upstairs to a hotel room.

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'look', paired with 'смотреть'.

examples.text: Можно я посмотрю?
examples.trans: May I have a look?

examples.text: Я только посмотрел.
examples.trans: I only had a look.

examples.text: А можно я пойду посмотрю?
examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'круг').

examples.text: Ты только посмотри, вокруг все рыжие!
examples.trans: Just look, everyone around here is red-headed!

examples.text: Она вокруг меня бегала.
examples.trans: She was running after me (around me).

examples.text: Посмотри вокруг.
examples.trans: Look around.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'all', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Вот этот отель весь принадлежит ей!
examples.trans: This entire hotel belongs to her!

examples.text: Нет, не слишком, ведь это инвестиция.
examples.trans: No, not too much, because it is an investment.

examples.text: Ах ты бессовестный негодяй, я тебя убью!
examples.trans: Oh you shameless scoundrel, I will kill you!

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('red-haired, ginger, rust-coloured').

examples.text: Ты только посмотри, вокруг все рыжие!
examples.trans: Just look, everyone around here is red-headed!

examples.text: Марина, скажите, в кого ваш мальчик такой рыжий?
examples.trans: Marina, tell me, who does your boy get that red hair from?

examples.text: У нас живёт рыжий кот.
examples.trans: A ginger cat lives with us.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сеня, ты чего там вдруг завис?
examples.trans: Senya, why did you freeze up over there?

examples.text: Шеф, вы не хотите мне палец сломать?
examples.trans: Chef, would you like to break my finger?

examples.text: Не будешь работать, я тебе спину сломаю!
examples.trans: If you do not work, I will break your back!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Сеня, ты чего там вдруг завис?
examples.trans: Senya, why did you freeze up over there?

examples.text: Я четыре года назад порезал себе палец.
examples.trans: Four years ago I cut my finger.

examples.text: И за четыре года нет ни одной царапины.
examples.trans: And in four years he has not had a single scratch.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'such, like this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну да, именно так я и предлагаю.
examples.trans: Well yes, that is exactly what I am proposing.

examples.text: Иди ты в баню с такой помощью!
examples.trans: Get lost with that kind of help!

examples.text: Ведь он тебе всё-таки родной отец.
examples.trans: After all, he is still your own father.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'казание'). Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'punishment, penalty' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: И за что мне такое наказание?
examples.trans: And what did I do to deserve such punishment?

examples.text: Суровое наказание.
examples.trans: A harsh punishment.

examples.text: Не надо никаких наказаний.
examples.trans: No need for any punishments.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'емья'). Common feminine noun meaning 'family' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: За его пустую голову дадут совсем немного.
examples.trans: They will give very little for his empty head.

examples.text: Неужели ты снова об этом совсем забыл?
examples.trans: Could you really have completely forgotten about it again?

examples.text: Старость — это совсем не радость, друзья.
examples.trans: Old age is no joy at all, my friends.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real').

examples.text: Это не семья, а настоящий пожар!
examples.trans: This is not a family, it is a real fire!

examples.text: Папа, ты настоящий герой нашей семьи!
examples.trans: Dad, you are a true hero of our family!

examples.text: Это настоящий успех!
examples.trans: This is real success!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'fire' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Здравствуйте, дорогие гости, добро пожаловать!
examples.trans: Hello, dear guests, welcome!

examples.text: Это не семья, а настоящий пожар!
examples.trans: This is not a family, it is a real fire!

examples.text: Там начался пожар!
examples.trans: A fire started there!
